DarmaH [ Driyate loko'nena, Darati lokaM vA Df-man;
cf. Uṇ. 1. 137]
1 Religion the customary observances of a caste sect, &c.
2 Law, usage, practice custom, ordinance, statute.
3
Religious or moral merit, virtue, righteousness, good works (regarded as one of the four ends of human existence); Ku. 5. 38 and see trivarga also; eka eva suhfdDarmo niDane'pyanuyAti yaH H. 1. 65.
4 Duty, prescribed course of conduct; zazWAMSavftterapi Darma ezaH Ś. 5. 4;Ms. 1. 114.
5 Right, justice, equity, impartiality.
6 Piety, propriety, decorum.
7
Morality, ethics.
8 Nature, disposition, character; Māl. 1. 6;prARi°, jIva°.
9 An essential quality, peculiarity, characteristic property, (peculiar) attribute; vadaMti varRyAvarRyAnAM DarmEkyaM dIpakaM buDAH Chandr. 5. 45; Pt. 1. 304.
10 Manner, resemblance, likeness.
11 A sacrifice.
12 Good company, associating with the virtuous.
13 Devotion, religious abstraction.
14 Manner, mode.
15 An Upaniṣad
q. v.
16
N. of
(
pb) Yudhiṣṭhira, the eldest Pāṇḍava.
17
N. of Yama, the god of death.
18 A bow.
19 A drinker of Soma juice.
20 (In
astrol.)
N. of the ninth lunar mansion.
21 An Arhat of the Jainas.
22 The soul.

m. a judge, magistrate, any judicial functionary.

— aDyakzaH
1 a judge.
2 an epithet of Viṣṇu.

conformity to virtue or justice.
— apeta
a. deviating from virtue, wicked, immoral, irreligious. (
— taM) vice, immorality, injustice.
— araRyaM a sacred or penance grove, a wood inhabited by ascetics; DarmAraRyaM
praviSati gajaH Ś. 1. 33.
— arTaM
ind.
1 for religious purposes.
2 justly, according to justice or right.
— alIka
a. having a false character.
— AgamaH a religious statute, lawbook.
— AcAryaH
1 a religious teacher.
2 a teacher of law or customs.

q. v.

a. just, righteous, pious, virtuous. (

— astikAyaH (with Jainas) the category or predicament of virtue;
cf. astikAya.
— iMdraH an epithet of Yudhishṭhira.
— ISaH an epithet of Yama.
— uttara
a. ‘rich in virtue’, chiefly characterized by justice, eminently just and impartial; DarmottaraM maDyamamASrayaMte R. 13. 7.
— upadeSaH
1 instruction in law or duty, religious or moral instruction.
2 the collective body of laws.
— upadeSakaH
(
pb)
1 a teacher of the law.
2 a spiritual teacher, a Guru.

n. ,
— kAryaM,

2 virtuous conduct.
— kaTAdaridraH the Kali age.
— kAma
a.
1 devoted to virtue.
2 observing duty or right.
— kAyaH
1 an epithet of Buddha.

1 Bharatavarṣa (the land of religion).
2
N. of a plain near Delhi, the scene of the great battle between the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas; Darmakzetre kurukzetre samavetA yuyutsavaH Bg. 1. 1. (
— traH) a virtuous or pious man.

— cAriRI
1 a wife.
2 a chaste or virtuous wife.
— ciMtaka
a.
1 studying or familiar with duty.
2 reflecting on the law.

cf. Ms. 9. 107.
2
N. of yuDizWira.

N. of yuDizWira.

a. one who acts according to the rules of his caste or fulfils prescribed duties. (
— naH) a Brāhmaṇa who maintains himself by assisting other men in the performance of their religious rites.
(
pb)
— jYa
a.
1 knowing what is right, conversant with civil or religious law; Ms. 7. 141,8. 179,10. 127.
2 just, righteous, pious.
— tyAgaH abandoning one's religion, apostacy.
— dAnaM a charitable gift (made without any self-interest.)
— duGA a cow milked for religious purposes only.

N. of the Ganges.
— dArAH (
m.
pl.) a lawful wife; strIRAM BartA DarmadArASca puMsAM Māl. 6. 18.
— drohin
m. a demon.
— DAtuH an epithet of Buddha.
— DvajaH, -Dvajin
m. a religious hypocrite, an impostor.
— naMdanaH an epithet of yuDizWira.
— nATaH a legal protector, rightful master.
— nABaH an epithet of Viṣṇu.
— nibaMDin
a. pious, holy.
— niveSaH
religious devotion.

f.
1 discharge or fulfilment of duty.
2 moral or religious observance.

— paTaH the way of virtue, a virtuous course of conduct.
— para
a. religiously-minded, pious, righteous.
— pAWakaH a teacher of civil or religious law.
— pAlaH
‘protector of the law,’ said metaphorically of (daMqa) ‘punishment or chastisement,’ or ‘sword’.
— pIqA transgressing the law, an offence against law.
— putraH
1 a lawful son, a son begotten from a sense of duty and not from mere lust or sensual pleasure.
2 an epithet of yuDizWira.
3 any one regarded as a son for religious purposes, a spiritual son.
— pravaktf
m.
1 an expounder of the law, a legal adviser.
2 a religious teacher, preacher.
— pravacanaM
1 the science of duty; U. 5. 23.
2 expounding the law. (
— naH) an epithet of Buddha.
— bARijikaH,
— vARijikaH
1 one who tries to make profit out of his virtue like a merchant.
2 one who performs religious rites with a view to reward, like a merchant dealing in transactions for profit.
— BaginI
1 a lawful sister.
2 a daughter of the spiritual preceptor.
3 a spiritual sister, any one regarded as a sister from discharging the same religious duties.
— BAginI a virtuous wife.
— BARakaH a lecturer or public reader who reads and explains to audiences sacred books like the Bhārata, Bhāgavata,
(
pb) &c.
— BikzukaH a mendicant from virtuous motives.
— Bft
m.
1 ‘a preserver or defender of justice,’ a king.
2 a virtuous person.
— BrAtf
m.
1 a fellow religious student, a spiritual brother.
2 any one regarded as a brother from discharging the same religious duties.
— mahAmAtraH a minister of religion, a minister in charge of religious affairs.
— mUlaM the foundation of civil or religious law, the Vedas.
— yugaM the Kṛta age.
— yUpaH an epithet of Viṣṇu.
— rati
a.
‘delighting in virtue or justice’, righteous, pious, just; R. 1. 23.
— rAj
m. an epithet of Yama.
— rAjaH an epithet of
1 Yama.
2 Jina.
3 yuDizWira.

m.

— roDin
a.
1 opposed to law, illegal' unlawful.
2 immoral.
— lakzaRaM
1 the essential mark of law.
2 the Vedas. (
— RA) the Mīmāṃsā philosophy.
— lopaH
1 irreligion, immorality.
2 violation of duty; R. 1. 76.
— vatsala
a. loving piety or duty.
— vartin a just, virtuous.
— varDanaH an epithet of Śiva.
— vAdaH discussion about law or duty, religious controversy.
— vAsaraH the day of full moon.
— vAhanaH

2 a buffalo (being the vehicle of Yama).

familiar with the law (civil or religious). °uttamaH

— viplavaH violation of duty, immorality.
— vivecanaM
1 judicial investigation.
2 dissertation on duty.

— SIla

— saMgaH
1 attachment to justice or virtue.
2 hypocrisy.
(
pb)

1 discussion about law.
2 (with Buddhists) a council.
